Lessons.Title: Two or More Lines
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will identify and draw parallel and intersecting lines.
In previous lessons, you identified and drew rays, lines, and segments. In this lesson, you turn your attention to lines that intersect , or cross, and those that never do. In the first activity, you draw two kinds of quadrilaterals, one of which is a rectangle.

2021 lesson activities: Warm-up: How Many Do You See: A Curious Figure (10 minutes); Activity 1: Four Lines (15 minutes); Activity 2: To Cross or Not to Cross (20 minutes); Cool-down: Parallel and Not Quite Parallel (5 minutes)
Corrected mathematical focus: Parallel lines in a plane never meet; intersecting lines share at least one point.

Edulytics authored guidance: On the original dot field identify the intersecting lines that form a triangle. Draw another line and reason whether the intersections produce the requested quadrilateral. On the second dot field label one line h and another line g, then describe their intersection.
First-party Cool-down (not publisher assessment): Draw one pair of parallel lines and one intersecting pair, labelling each.
Images, drawing/protractor accuracy, partner tasks and the gated original publisher Cool-down require original task evidence and teacher/visual review.
